title: Working at Redwood — roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring, onboarding, and internal tools
author: Samantha Chen
body:
Overview

This page consolidates the most-used sections of the Redwood employee handbook into a single reference for: working at Redwood, role and career ladder expectations, benefits & perks, high-level hiring and onboarding flow, and the primary internal tools and access patterns. Use the links in the related pages field for detailed policies and the People Ops wiki for forms and request templates.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Introduction
- Redwood is a fast-moving, engineering-first company focused on delivering reliable, cost-effective inference for customers. Our culture values ownership, clear communication, and customer-focused product thinking.
- Every employee is expected to follow our company values (ownership, collaboration, learning, and reliability), proactively communicate blockers, and participate in continuous improvement.

Work model and hours
- Hybrid-first model: teams are trusted to set their in-office cadence. Typical expectation is 2-3 days/week in office for cross-functional collaboration unless role-specific accommodations are agreed.
- Core hours: 10:00-16:00 local time for overlapping collaboration; flexible outside those hours.

Communication norms
- Use Slack for day-to-day communication; create public channels for project-level discussion. Reserve email for cross-company announcements, legal/finance correspondence, and external communications.
- Document decisions and designs in Confluence. Significant architecture or product decisions should have an ADR and a decision owner.

Performance reviews and feedback
- Quarterly OKR check-ins with manager; formal performance calibration twice per year. Expect continuous feedback cycles and one structured skip-level check per year.

2) Roles & Career ladders — how we level and grow

Overview
- Redwood uses structured career ladders for the primary disciplines: Engineering (Infra, Runtime, Platform, SRE), Product, Design, Data & Applied ML, Sales/Customer Success, and People Ops. Each ladder has clear level descriptions, core expectations, and example competencies.

Quick reference table — levels and focus
- | Level | Typical title examples | Primary focus |
- | L1 | Associate / IC1 | Execute on tasks with manager support |
- | L2 | IC2 / Software Engineer | Deliver components independently |
- | L3 | Senior / Staff Engineer | System design, mentorship, cross-team impact |
- | L4 | Principal / Lead | Strategy, multiple-service ownership, org-level influence |
- | L5 | Director+ | People and product leadership, multi-team strategy |

Engineering ladder highlights
- L3 (Senior): owns feature lifecycle from design to rollout, writes ADRs, mentors junior engineers, contributes to cross-team reliability goals.
- L4 (Principal): sets architecture on critical subsystems (serving runtime, scheduler), leads postmortem and reliability initiatives, influences roadmap and capacity planning.

Promotion process and calibration
- Promotions are nomination-based: manager initiates packet with evidence (projects, metrics, feedback). People Ops schedules calibration panel; panel evaluates against ladder rubric. Typical timeline: 6-12 weeks.

Career development resources
- Learning stipend: $2,000/year for conferences, training, and books. Mentorship program and engineering guilds provide peer coaching.

3) Benefits & perks — summary of what Redwood provides

Health and wellbeing
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contributions. Detailed plan documents and enrollment instructions are in the People Ops benefits portal.
- Mental health: confidential EAP (Employee Assistance Program) and paid therapy sessions coverage.

Compensation & equity
- Competitive base salary with regular market adjustments. Equity grants for all full-time employees with standard 4-year vesting and 1-year cliff. Performance bonuses or discretionary grants may be available based on role and level.

Paid time off and leaves
- PTO: flexible vacation policy (coordinate with manager); recommended minimum of 3 weeks/year.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (paid). Additional unpaid or partial-paid leaves follow local statutory requirements.

Remote & office support
- Home office stipend: $500 on hire + $300/year for equipment. Hot-desking available at offices; reserved desks for those with accommodation needs.

Perks and team budgets
- Stipend for internet/mobile, wellness (gym/fitness), and team offsites. Annual learning stipend noted above. Monthly lunch & learn budget per team.

4) High-level hiring process & candidate experience

Phases (standard loop for IC engineering roles)
- 1) Recruiter screen: match on basic qualifications and candidate questions.
- 2) Hiring manager screen: team fit and background deep-dive.
- 3) Technical take-home or work sample (optional based on role).
- 4) Onsite / virtual interview loop: 4-5 interviews (system design, coding, product sense / applied ML, culture & collaboration).
- 5) Hiring committee review and offer approval.
- 6) Reference checks and background checks (for certain roles).

Interviewer guidance and fairness
- Interviewers must complete unconscious bias training annually. Use the standardized rubrics (available in the hiring toolkit) and provide written feedback within 48 hours of the interview.

Offer and negotiation
- Offers are reviewed by People Ops and the hiring committee. Compensation bands are published internally; managers consult People Ops for exceptional cases. Equity, sign-on, and relocation packages are included when applicable.

5) Onboarding & first-90-days checklist

Pre-boarding (before start date)
- Complete HR forms, benefits enrollment, and equipment request via People Ops portal.
- Receive welcome packet, team org chart, and initial 30/60/90 suggested goals from manager.

Day 0-7
- IT setup: Okta SSO, company email, Slack, GitHub access, Confluence access.
- Introductory meetings: manager 1:1, buddy assignment, and team kickoff.
- Safety & compliance training modules (security, data handling) must be completed within the first week.

Week 2-4
- Execute first onboarding projects: small bug fix or docs improvement to learn the codebase and deployment flow. Attend product and architecture overview sessions.

Month 1-3
- Quarterly objectives: deliver a scoped feature, present a short retrofit/learnings talk to the team, complete two cross-team touchpoints. Manager will run weekly 1:1s and a 30/60/90 review at 30 and 90 days.

Buddy program and mentoring
- New hires are assigned a buddy for the first 90 days for technical and cultural orientation. Guilds and cross-team office hours are available for deeper onboarding.

6) Internal tools & access guide

Core tools (what we use and who to contact)
- Slack — primary chat for teams and channels. Public channels for project discoverability. Admins: @it-ops.
- Google Workspace — email, drive, calendar. Shared team drives are used for cross-team documents. Admins: People Ops.
- Confluence — internal documentation and ADRs. Naming convention: <team>/<topic>/<date> (example: eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture-2026-03-04).
- GitHub — code hosting, PRs, branch protection. Use main->release branching + protected releases for production-deployable services.
- Jira — issue tracking, sprint planning. Product & Eng teams use story points and standard issue types.
- Okta — SSO & identity. Use Okta to request app access and for MFA enrollment.
- Redwood Console (internal) — internal dashboards for billing, infra capacity, and deployment status (read-only for most employees, write access by request). Contact: platform-oncall@redwood.ai.
- VPN / Bastion access — required for certain private deploys and on-prem administration. Request via Infra Access form; approval depends on role and manager.

Access requests and deprovisioning
- All access requests go through the IT access form (Confluence link in People Ops portal). Managers must approve requests. New access takes up to 48 hours.
- Offboarding: People Ops initiates deprovisioning on last day; managers must return equipment and confirm knowledge transfer.

Common CLI / config snippets
- Git: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/<repo>.git
- GitHub: create a branch from main: git checkout -b <team>/<ticket-id>-short-desc
- Deploy (example internal service): rwctl deploy --service serving-runtime --env staging --version <sha>

Security & data handling reminders
- Treat all customer data as sensitive. Follow the data handling playbook in security-and-compliance. Do not copy customer data to personal accounts.
- MFA is required for all accounts; rotate SSH keys annually and register keys with your GitHub profile.

7) Quick reference tables and templates

Role expectation matrix (short)
- | Area | IC2 | Senior (L3) | Principal (L4) |
- | Delivery | Delivers features with review | Owns features end-to-end | Owns multi-service initiatives |
- | Design | Implements designs | Proposes and documents designs | Drives architecture and tradeoffs |
- | Mentorship | Peer feedback | Mentors junior engineers | Builds mentoring programs |

Onboarding 30/60/90 template (to share with new hires)
- 30 days: Complete security & infra training, merge first small PR, meet 8 cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: Deliver first scoped feature, give a demo to team, set career goals with manager.
- 90 days: Lead a post-launch review, submit promotion development plan if applicable, and present a learnings talk.

8) Owners and escalation

Document owner
- People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai) owns this handbook page and maintenance.

Escalations
- For benefits and payroll issues: payroll@redwood.ai.
- For IT or access problems: it-support@redwood.ai.
- For security incidents: security@redwood.ai (follow incident response runbook in security-and-compliance).

Appendix: links & forms (internal)
- People Ops portal: /confluence/people-ops/benefits-enrollment
- Hiring toolkit (interview guides & rubrics): /confluence/hiring/hiring-toolkit
- IT access request form: /confluence/it/access-request-form

If you have feedback or suggested updates to this page, add a comment or contact People Ops directly.
